title: Duplicate dispatch across contact channels
source_story: User-provided fictional owner stories in this conversation; opening narrative below is a faithful condensed adaptation, not a verbatim transcript.
business_context: 14 staff; nine field technicians; approximately 90 office and school customers; monthly maintenance with some parts extra.
owner_narrative: Teachers contact our office, their usual technician, or me. Our office uses Excel and group chat. Two technicians attended the same printer after different teachers described the problem differently. Other requests disappear because everybody assumes somebody else accepted them. Customers will keep calling, so a mandatory customer portal will not solve this alone.
current_workflow: Customer reports by phone or message

diagnostic_interview.question: Were both visits for the same device and fault?
diagnostic_interview.synthetic_answer: A serial-number photo and visit notes identify the same printer; both describe an offline queue.
diagnostic_interview.diagnostic_value: Distinguishes an unnecessary duplicate from legitimate parallel work.
diagnostic_interview.branch_if_answer_differs: If both assignments were visible and intentionally required different skills, deduplication would be wrong; examine assignment reasons before merging.

diagnostic_interview.question: Were both requests visible before assignment?
diagnostic_interview.synthetic_answer: The direct message remained on the regular technician’s phone until after arrival.
diagnostic_interview.diagnostic_value: Locates the failure before dispatch rather than in routing.
diagnostic_interview.branch_if_answer_differs: Revise the causal hypothesis and request the corresponding source record; do not reuse this fictional answer for a new customer.

diagnostic_interview.question: Who can accept a direct request?
diagnostic_interview.synthetic_answer: Technicians promise a visit without informing the coordinator.
diagnostic_interview.branch_if_answer_differs: Revise the causal hypothesis and request the corresponding source record; do not reuse this fictional answer for a new customer.

diagnostic_interview.question: Can staff record an incomplete request?
diagnostic_interview.synthetic_answer: The current sheet expects a device model, which callers often do not know.
diagnostic_interview.diagnostic_value: Missing optional data must not prevent intake.
diagnostic_interview.branch_if_answer_differs: Revise the causal hypothesis and request the corresponding source record; do not reuse this fictional answer for a new customer.

evidence.description: Simulated incident D-101 contains two reporter messages and one device serial.
Simulated dispatch timeline shows the second assignment before the first message entered the shared log.
A simulated coordinator interview confirms no shared acceptance rule.

diagnoses.hypothesis: Requests and commitments bypass the shared queue; asset ambiguity makes the bypass harder to detect.
diagnoses.counterhypothesis: If both assignments were visible and intentionally required different skills, deduplication would be wrong; examine assignment reasons before merging.
diagnoses.confidence_policy: Qualitative case-world support only; requires fresh customer evidence before reuse.

interventions.process_first: Nominate the coordinator as assignment owner; require a short direct-contact capture before promising attendance, allowing an urgent exception with later reconciliation.
interventions.deterministic_and_assisted_automation: Create intake drafts from supported channels; show related open incidents and active assignments; require a coordinator decision on ambiguous duplicates.
interventions.rejected_default: Do not replace the whole service platform or deploy autonomous agents solely because the owner reports inefficiency.
interventions.selection_basis: Choose the least complex intervention addressing the supported handoff failure; compare added administration and integration burden.

requirements.statement: Never merge solely on school name or textual similarity.
requirements.rationale: Requests and commitments bypass the shared queue; asset ambiguity makes the bypass harder to detect.

requirements.statement: Preserve original reports and their reporters after a merge.
requirements.rationale: Requests and commitments bypass the shared queue; asset ambiguity makes the bypass harder to detect.

requirements.statement: Commit assignments with an incident version check; a second worker requires an explicit reason.

requirements.statement: Unknown asset identity routes to clarification, not silent rejection.

acceptance_tests.scenario_and_expected_result: Two descriptions with a verified common serial surface together before dispatch.
Two different printers at one school remain separate.
Concurrent dispatch attempts produce one accepted assignment and one conflict to review.

capability_boundary.proposed_extension: Cross-channel identity resolution and transactional assignment safeguards need separate implementation.
capability_boundary.pricing: No price assigned; current rate card must not be extended by analogy.

evaluation.primary_metric_definition: Unnecessary duplicate dispatches / all dispatched incidents; adjudicate duplicates using device, work and timing evidence, excluding planned multi-person jobs.
measurement_cautions: Use a stable denominator and comparable operating periods.
Record missingness and changed case mix.
Do not infer staff reductions from reclaimed task minutes.

implementation.baseline: Collect at least one representative operating cycle before rollout; for monthly billing or maintenance include the relevant full cycle. Extend sampling when volumes or seasonality make the sample unrepresentative.
implementation.scope: Start with one consenting customer group and the staff who own its handoffs; include a normal case and each listed exception.
sequence: Reconcile identities and existing obligations with the process owner.
Run the proposed rules in shadow mode; record disagreements and missed exceptions.
Approve a bounded live pilot only after requirements and exceptions have named owners.
Review outcome metrics, added administrative work and failure logs before expanding.
implementation.simulated_resolution: In this fictional case, MILO introduced the process change: Nominate the coordinator as assignment owner; require a short direct-contact capture before promising attendance, allowing an urgent exception with later reconciliation. The team adopted the proposed workflow for the pilot scope. Routine coordination became explicit; unresolved exceptions continued to require a person.
implementation.simulated_lesson: If both assignments were visible and intentionally required different skills, deduplication would be wrong; examine assignment reasons before merging.
implementation.rollback: Pause automated writes and notifications, retain the event log, export outstanding work and return to a named manual coordinator. Reconcile queued events before resuming to avoid duplicate actions.
implementation.go_no_go: Process owner reviews coverage of acceptance cases, unresolved critical failures, metric direction and staff workload. No fixed performance threshold is claimed without customer agreement.

open_questions: Channel capture permissions and a practical direct-call logging method are unverified.
